title: flixpatrol 1.1.0
text:
TV content is now labelled "tvshow" instead of "tv_show" in the type column of every function’s output. Inputs still accept "tv", "tv show", "tv_show", "tvshow" and their plurals.
validate_date_format() is no longer exported.
Removed get_franchise_performance(). The API’s franchise response does not list a franchise’s titles, so the function could only return an empty result.





country_name = "Global" covers about 45 countries in lookup_country(), get_top_ten() and get_official_ranking(). Both add a country column. Each country is a separate set of requests, so a run can take many minutes: a message at the start gives the minimum time, and a warning at the end lists any country that failed or returned no rows, with the reason.





"TV Show" and "tv shows" (with a space) were not recognised as TV content.
get_top_ten() now warns when a request fails, instead of stopping with an unrelated error.
get_torrent_ranking() filters media_type after the request, because the API does not support filtering torrents by type.





The title is now “Client for the ‘FlixPatrol’ Streaming Rankings API”, and the Description links to the API documentation.
Tests that call the API are skipped on CRAN, so CRAN checks make no network requests.
:= is imported from ‘rlang’.

title: Getting Started with flixpatrol
text: This article demonstrates how to use the flixpatrol package to retrieve streaming platform rankings and analytics from the FlixPatrol API. The code here is not run when the site is built. The #> lines show results where they are fixed, such as IDs, and otherwise list the columns you get back.

title: Getting Started with flixpatrol
text:
Setup
First, load the package and set your API key:

library(flixpatrol)

# Set your API key (do this once in your .Renviron)
usethis::edit_r_environ()
# Add: FLIX_PATROL=your_api_key_here

To suppress lookup messages globally:

options(flixpatrol.silent = TRUE)

title: Getting Started with flixpatrol
text:
Looking Up IDs
Before fetching data, you often need to translate human-readable names to FlixPatrol IDs.

Countries and Platforms

# Single lookup
lookup_platform("Netflix")
#> [1] "cmp_IA6TdMqwf6kuyQvxo9bJ4nKX"

# Multiple at once (vectorized)
lookup_platform(c("Netflix", "Disney+", "HBO Max"))
#> [1] "cmp_IA6TdMqwf6kuyQvxo9bJ4nKX" "cmp_oGtsgdpOrjIu3XzTEnWPt87Y"
#> [3] "cmp_6UhCvnTeRkgZUtcNGslX9bJL"

lookup_country(c("United States", "Germany", "Japan"))



Titles and Franchises

lookup_title("Squid Game")
#> [1] "ttl_c0MNOjICD0BkFTWeZEXR41y5"

lookup_franchise("Indiana Jones")
#> [1] "frn_STNa2GEw54ahWxJsXNgBMmt0"



Reverse Lookup (ID to Name)

# Works with any ID type (cmp_, ttl_, frn_)
get_title_name("cmp_IA6TdMqwf6kuyQvxo9bJ4nKX")
#> [1] "Netflix"

# Vectorized - returns NA for failures
get_title_name(c("cmp_IA6TdMqwf6kuyQvxo9bJ4nKX", "ttl_invalid"))
#> [1] "Netflix" NA

title: Getting Started with flixpatrol
text:
Fetching Top 10 Rankings

Daily Top 10

# Get a week of Top 10 data
top10 <- get_top_ten(
  platform_name = "netflix",
  country_name  = "United States",
  start_date    = "2025-12-01",
  end_date      = "2025-12-07",
  media_type    = "movie"
)

names(top10)
#> [1] "rank"       "title"      "type"       "days_total" "rank_last"
#> [6] "date"       "imdb_id"



All Countries
country_name = "Global" covers about 45 countries and adds a country column. Each country is requested separately, so a call takes at least 14 minutes at the default throttle of 10 requests per minute and uses far more API quota. A warning lists any country that failed or returned no rows. get_official_ranking() accepts it too.

get_top_ten(
  platform_name = "netflix",
  country_name  = "Global",
  start_date    = "2025-12-15",
  end_date      = "2025-12-15",
  media_type    = "movie"
)



Filtering Results

library(dplyr)

# Find #1 movies each day
top10 |>
  filter(rank == 1) |>
  select(date, title, days_total)

# Titles that appeared multiple days
top10 |>
  count(title, sort = TRUE) |>
  filter(n > 3)

title: Getting Started with flixpatrol
text:
Viewing Hours Data
Netflix publishes weekly viewing hours, Monday to Sunday. A start_date that is not a Monday moves forward to the next Monday:

hours <- get_hours_viewed(
  platform_name   = "netflix",
  language_name   = "english",
  media_type      = "movie",
  start_date      = "2025-12-15",
  end_date        = "2025-12-21"
)

names(hours)
#> [1] "rank"      "title"     "hours"     "views"     "runtime"   "streak"
#> [7] "date_from" "date_to"

hours |>
  select(title, hours) |>
  arrange(desc(hours))

title: Getting Started with flixpatrol
text:
Premieres
Get upcoming releases for a platform:

premieres <- get_premieres(
  platform_name = "netflix",
  start_date    = "2025-12-01",
  end_date      = "2025-12-31"
)

names(premieres)
#> [1] "title"    "imdb_id"  "premiere" "type"     "season"   "episodes"
#> [7] "binge"    "platform"

premieres |>
  select(title, premiere, type) |>
  arrange(premiere)

title: Getting Started with flixpatrol
text:
Analytics Functions

Compare Across Platforms
See how a title performs on different streaming services:

compare_platforms(
  title      = "Stranger Things",
  date       = "2025-12-01",
  platforms  = c("netflix", "disney+", "hbo max", "amazon prime"),
  media_type = "tvshow"
)
# One row per platform, with an NA rank where the title is not in the Top 10.
# Columns: platform, rank, title, type, days_total, rank_last, date, imdb_id



Track a Title Over Time

history <- get_title_history(
  title         = "Stranger Things",
  platform_name = "netflix",
  country_name  = "United States",
  start_date    = "2025-12-01",
  end_date      = "2025-12-07",
  media_type    = "tvshow"
)

names(history)
#> [1] "rank"       "title"      "type"       "days_total" "rank_last"
#> [6] "date"       "imdb_id"



Weekly Movers
Identify which titles gained or lost positions:

movers <- get_weekly_movers(
  platform_name = "netflix",
  country_name  = "United States",
  date_before   = "2025-12-14",
  date_after    = "2025-12-15",
  media_type    = "movie"
)

names(movers)
#> [1] "title"       "rank_before" "rank_after"  "change"      "status"

# status is one of: new_entry, exit, gainer, loser, unchanged
movers |>
  filter(status %in% c("gainer", "new_entry")) |>
  arrange(desc(change))



Top Titles Summary
Summarize which titles dominated over a period:

summary_tbl <- get_top_titles_summary(
  platform_name = "netflix",
  country_name  = "United States",
  start_date    = "2025-12-01",
  end_date      = "2025-12-31",
  media_type    = "movie",
  n             = 10
)

names(summary_tbl)
#> [1] "title"         "days_on_chart" "best_rank"     "avg_rank"
#> [5] "first_seen"    "last_seen"



Global Ranking
See how a title ranks in different countries:

global <- get_global_ranking(
  title         = "Stranger Things",
  platform_name = "netflix",
  date          = "2025-12-01",
  media_type    = "tvshow"
)

names(global)
#> [1] "country"    "rank"       "title"      "type"       "days_total"
#> [6] "rank_last"  "date"       "imdb_id"

global |>
  filter(!is.na(rank)) |>
  arrange(rank)

title: Create a Daily Top 10 Table for a Date Range
text:
Details

The ‘/top10s’ endpoint supports date range queries but limits results to 300 records per call. This function automatically chunks large date ranges into 30-day periods and combines the results.

title: Create a Daily Top 10 Table for a Date Range
text:
Global


‘country_name = “Global”’ makes separate requests for each of about 45 countries, one at a time, so a call can take many minutes at the default throttle of 10 requests per minute and uses far more of your API quota than one country. A message at the start gives the minimum time. Countries that fail or return no rows are left out of the result and listed in a warning. Change the rate with ‘options(flixpatrol.throttle_rate = …)’.

Source: R/api.R
Fetches the official weekly rankings (currently Netflix exclusive).

title: Create Official Ranking Table
text:
Usage
get_official_ranking(
  platform_name = "netflix",
  country_name = getOption("flixpatrol.country_name"),
  start_date = getOption("flixpatrol.start_date"),
  end_date = getOption("flixpatrol.end_date"),
  media_type = getOption("flixpatrol.media_type"),
  date_type = "week",
  language = getOption("flixpatrol.language", "english"),
  return_ids = getOption("flixpatrol.return_ids", FALSE)
)

title: Create Official Ranking Table
text:
Arguments


platform_name



Character. Must be “netflix”.



country_name



Character. Name of the country (e.g., “United States”). Default from ‘getOption(“flixpatrol.country_name”)’.



start_date



Character. Range start in yyyy-mm-dd format. Does not need to be a Monday; if not, it will be adjusted to the next Monday automatically. Default from ‘getOption(“flixpatrol.start_date”)’.



end_date



Character. Range end in yyyy-mm-dd format. The function will include any week where the Monday falls on or before this date. Default from ‘getOption(“flixpatrol.end_date”)’.



media_type



Character. Content type (“movie” or “tvshow”). Default from ‘getOption(“flixpatrol.media_type”)’.



date_type



Character. Defaults to “week”.



language



Character. Language for lookup (e.g., “english”). Default from ‘getOption(“flixpatrol.language”, “english”)’.



return_ids



Logical. Include ID columns in output. Default from ‘getOption(“flixpatrol.return_ids”, FALSE)’.

title: Create Official Ranking Table
text:
Value

A tibble with columns: rank, title, hours, streak, date_from, date_to. If ‘return_ids = TRUE’, also includes title_id. Each row represents a title’s ranking for a specific week. Multiple weeks will have multiple rows per title.

title: Create Official Ranking Table
text:
Details

Queries the ‘/rankingsofficial’ endpoint. Note that as of the current package version, FlixPatrol only provides official lists for Netflix.

title: Create Official Ranking Table
text:
Date Range Handling


The function accepts any date range spanning days, months, or years and automatically fetches all weekly rankings within that period. The API requires 7-day Monday-to-Sunday periods, so the function handles this internally:



If ‘start_date’ is not a Monday, it is adjusted forward to the next Monday
A sequence of Mondays is generated from start to end date
For each Monday, the corresponding Sunday is calculated (Monday + 6 days)
Each Monday-Sunday pair is queried from the API
All results are combined into a single tibble



For example, if you provide ‘start_date = “2024-01-01”’ and ‘end_date = “2024-01-31”’, the function will fetch rankings for: - 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 - 2024-01-08 to 2024-01-14 - 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-21 - 2024-01-22 to 2024-01-28 - 2024-01-29 to 2024-02-04

title: Create Official Ranking Table
text:
Global


‘country_name = “Global”’ makes separate requests for each of about 45 countries, one at a time, so a call can take many minutes at the default throttle of 10 requests per minute and uses far more of your API quota than one country. A message at the start gives the minimum time. Countries that fail or return no rows are left out of the result and listed in a warning. Change the rate with ‘options(flixpatrol.throttle_rate = …)’.

title: Create Official Ranking Table
text:
Global Options


Parameters can be set globally using options so you don’t have to specify them on every call: - ‘options(flixpatrol.country_name = “United States”)’ - ‘options(flixpatrol.start_date = “2024-01-01”)’ - ‘options(flixpatrol.end_date = “2026-12-31”)’ - ‘options(flixpatrol.media_type = “movie”)’ - ‘options(flixpatrol.language = “english”)’ - ‘options(flixpatrol.return_ids = TRUE)’

title: Create Official Ranking Table
text:
Examples

# Fetch a single week
get_official_ranking(
  country_name = "United States",
  start_date   = "2024-01-01",
  end_date     = "2024-01-07",
  media_type   = "movie"
)

# Fetch multiple years of weekly rankings
get_official_ranking(
  country_name = "United States",
  start_date   = "2022-01-01",
  end_date     = "2024-12-31",
  media_type   = "movie"
)

# Set global options for repeated use
options(
  flixpatrol.country_name = "United States",
  flixpatrol.start_date   = "2024-01-01",
  flixpatrol.end_date     = "2026-02-14",
  flixpatrol.media_type   = "movie"
)

# Now call without arguments
get_official_ranking()

# Override specific options as needed
get_official_ranking(media_type = "tvshow")
get_official_ranking(country_name = "United Kingdom")

Citing this package




Alejandro Hagan (author, maintainer)
The flixpatrol package is an R interface for the FlixPatrol API V2. It allows for the programmatic retrieval of VOD rankings, streaming Top 10 lists, official viewing hour statistics, torrent charts, social media fan metrics, and premiere schedules across major global platforms.

title: flixpatrol
text:
Features

Metadata Lookup: Resolve country, platform, franchise, and title names into internal FlixPatrol IDs.
Historical Data Retrieval: Fetch daily Top 10 charts over custom date ranges.
Official Metrics: Access “Hours Viewed” and “Official Ranking” tables as analysis-ready tibbles.
Torrent Rankings: Pull torrent chart data by site and date range.
Social Media Fans: Retrieve fan count rankings from Instagram, Facebook, and Twitter.
Premieres: Get upcoming premiere schedules by platform and country.
Title Details: Retrieve full metadata for any title.
Vectorized ID Resolution: Resolve FlixPatrol IDs back to human-readable names in bulk.
Robust Validation: Built-in checks for date ranges and API-specific weekday requirements (e.g., weekly charts starting on Mondays).
Rate Limiting & Retry: All API calls are throttled (10 req/min) with automatic retry on transient failures.

title: flixpatrol
text:
Usage

Lookup Functions
Translate human-readable names into FlixPatrol internal IDs:
library(flixpatrol)

lookup_country("United States")
lookup_platform("Netflix")
lookup_franchise("Indiana Jones")
lookup_title("Squid Game")

# Vectorized
lookup_country(c("United States", "Germany", "Japan"))


Reverse Lookups (ID to Name)
get_title_name("cmp_IA6TdMqwf6kuyQvxo9bJ4nKX")  # company
get_title_name("ttl_yPCJU2UzROTNVv5JZ7Hu4m8M")  # title

# Vectorized - returns NA for failures
get_title_name(c("cmp_IA6TdMqwf6kuyQvxo9bJ4nKX", "ttl_invalid"))


Daily Top 10
get_top_ten(
  platform_name = "netflix",
  country_name  = "United States",
  start_date    = "2025-12-01",
  end_date      = "2025-12-07",
  media_type    = "movie"
)


Hours Viewed
Weekly data, Monday to Sunday. A start_date that is not a Monday moves forward to the next Monday:
get_hours_viewed(
  platform_name = "netflix",
  media_type    = "movie",
  language_name = "english",
  start_date    = "2025-12-15",
  end_date      = "2025-12-21"
)


All Countries
Pass country_name = "Global" to get_top_ten() or get_official_ranking() to cover about 45 countries and add a country column. Each country is requested separately, so this takes at least 14 minutes at the default throttle and uses far more API quota. A warning lists any country that failed or returned no rows.
get_top_ten(
  platform_name = "netflix",
  country_name  = "Global",
  start_date    = "2025-12-15",
  end_date      = "2025-12-15",
  media_type    = "movie"
)


Official Rankings (Netflix Only)
get_official_ranking(
  country_name = "United States",
  start_date   = "2025-12-15",
  end_date     = "2025-12-21",
  media_type   = "movie"
)


Torrent Rankings
get_torrent_ranking(
  torrent_site = "PirateBay",
  start_date   = "2025-12-01",
  end_date     = "2025-12-01"
)


Social Media Fans
get_fans_ranking(
  social_platform = "Instagram",
  start_date      = "2025-12-15",
  end_date        = "2025-12-21"
)


Premieres
get_premieres(
  platform_name = "netflix",
  start_date    = "2025-12-15",
  end_date      = "2025-12-31"
)


Title Details
get_title_details("ttl_yPCJU2UzROTNVv5JZ7Hu4m8M")


Compare Platforms
See how a title ranks across multiple platforms on the same day:
compare_platforms(
  title      = "Squid Game",
  date       = "2025-12-15",
  media_type = "tvshow"
)


Title History
Track a single title’s rank over time:
get_title_history(
  title      = "Squid Game",
  start_date = "2025-12-01",
  end_date   = "2025-12-14",
  media_type = "tvshow"
)


Weekly Movers
Identify gainers, losers, new entries, and exits between two chart dates:
get_weekly_movers(
  date_before = "2025-12-14",
  date_after  = "2025-12-15"
)


Top Titles Summary
Most frequent Top 10 titles over a date range with best/average rank:
get_top_titles_summary(
  start_date = "2025-12-01",
  end_date   = "2025-12-14",
  n          = 10
)


Global Ranking
See where a title ranks across 15 countries:
get_global_ranking(
  title      = "Squid Game",
  date       = "2025-12-15",
  media_type = "tvshow"
)

title: Developer’s Guide
text: This guide is for developers maintaining or contributing to the flixpatrol R package.

title: Developer’s Guide
text:
Package Overview
flixpatrol is an R interface for the FlixPatrol API V2. It provides functions to retrieve streaming platform rankings, viewing statistics, and metadata.

title: Developer’s Guide
text:
Codebase Structure
flixpatrol/
├── R/                      # Source code
│   ├── api.R               # Core functions (auth, lookups, data retrieval)
│   ├── utils-api.R         # API utility functions
│   └── utils-new.R         # Analytics and helper functions
├── data/                   # Pre-built lookup tables (.rda)
├── data-raw/               # Scripts to regenerate lookup tables
├── man/                    # Roxygen2-generated documentation
├── tests/testthat/         # Unit tests
├── docs/                   # Rendered website (qrtdown output)
├── vignettes/articles/     # Website-only articles (qrtdown builds these)
├── _qrtdown.yml            # qrtdown configuration
└── README.qmd              # Package homepage (becomes index.qmd)

title: Developer’s Guide
text:
Function Naming Conventions

Prefixes








Prefix
Purpose
Example




get_*
Fetch data from API
get_top_ten(), get_premieres()


lookup_*
Resolve names to IDs
lookup_country(), lookup_platform()


fp_*
Pipeline helpers
fp_enrich(), fp_cache_ids()





Guidelines

Use get_* for API data retrieval, not create_* or fetch_*
Use lookup_* for name-to-ID translation (returns character IDs)
Avoid redundant suffixes like _tbl or _and_return_id
All functions should be vectorized where possible

title: Developer’s Guide
text:
API Integration Patterns

Authentication
All API calls go through authenticate() which:

Reads the API key from Sys.getenv("FLIX_PATROL")
Uses httr2 basic auth
Applies rate limiting (10 requests/minute)
Enables automatic retry (5 attempts with exponential backoff)


authenticate(site = "https://api.flixpatrol.com/v2/endpoint")



Query Parameters
The FlixPatrol API uses bracket notation for filters:



Operator
Usage
Example




[eq]
Exact match
company[eq]=cmp_xxx


[in]
Match any in list
name[in]=Netflix


[nin]
Not in list
type[nin]=1


[gte]
Greater than or equal
premiere[gte]=2025-01-01


[lte]
Less than or equal
premiere[lte]=2025-12-31



Important: The API does NOT support [like] for fuzzy matching.


Response Handling
Use unnest_flixpatrol_response() to flatten nested JSON:

body <- httr2::resp_body_json(resp)
unnest_flixpatrol_response(body$data)

This helper conditionally unnests columns that exist, handling varying response structures.


Global Requests
country_name = "Global" goes through fetch_global(), which requests each country in global_countries() separately. It adds the country column, states the minimum run time from the throttle, and warns about any country that failed, returned no rows, or came back incomplete.

title: Developer’s Guide
Developer’s Guide
text:
Lookup Tables

Static Tables (in data/)
Used for values that don’t change:

flix_type_tbl - Content types
language_name - Languages
media_type_name - Media types
date_type_name - Date granularities
torrent_sites - Torrent site mappings
social_media_name - Social platform IDs



Regenerating Tables
Scripts in data-raw/ generate the .rda files:

source("data-raw/torrent.R")  # Fetches from API
source("data-raw/type.R")     # Hardcoded values

title: Developer’s Guide
text:
Package Options
Users can set global options:

options(flixpatrol.silent = TRUE)  # Suppress lookup messages

Add new options to flixpatrol_options() in api.R.

title: Developer’s Guide
text:
Testing

Running Tests

devtools::test()



Test Structure

Tests use testthat edition 3
Tests that make HTTP requests call skip_on_cran(), so CRAN checks make no network requests
Tests that need a real key also skip when FLIX_PATROL is not set. skip_if_no_api_key() is defined in test-lookup-api.R, so a new test file needs its own copy
Use withr::local_envvar() to set environment variables
Use httr2::local_mocked_responses() and local_mocked_bindings() to test without the network, as in test-global-countries.R



Writing Tests

describe("get_something()", {

    it("returns a tibble for valid input", {
        skip_on_cran()
        skip_if_no_api_key()
        result <- get_something("value")
        expect_s3_class(result, "tbl_df")
    })

    it("handles empty results gracefully", {
        skip_on_cran()
        skip_if_no_api_key()
        result <- get_something("nonexistent")
        expect_equal(nrow(result), 0)
    })
})
